bandReport.notes: Items 44-56 (13 items) across printed pages 27, 29, 31, 33. Column crops p26/p28/p30/p32 c1+c2 were all clean - no slicing, no stray fragments, no missing item numbers at the top of c2; nothing had to be read off the whole-page image. PASSAGE OUTSIDE THE BAND: item 44 says 'With reference to the passage' but its passage is printed on page index 24 (printed p.25), outside this band. That page carries 'Directions for the following 4 (four) items' over TWO passages - Passage-1 (leisure/overstrain) governs items 41-42, Passage-2 (demographic dividend) governs items 43-44. Item 44's statements are both about demographic dividend and higher education, so Passage-2 is its governing passage; I read page 24 and its c2 crop and have included that passage verbatim as item 44's context. WITHIN-BAND PASSAGES: page 30 (printed p.31) carries 'Directions for the following 3 (three) items' over two passages - Passage-1 (economic organization / leisure / education) governs item 51 ONLY; Passage-2 (presents and children's joys) governs items 52 AND 53. Item 53's stem is the bare 'The author of the passage is against', which is only answerable against Passage-2, and 52 and 53 are the 2nd and 3rd of the 3 items in that block. Per the shipped convention in 2023-p2.merged.json / 2025-p2.merged.json (which both contain single-item contexts) the single-item Passage-1 is still stored in context; there is no hash-collision risk because item 51's options are unique text. Neither the 'Directions...' preamble nor the 'Passage-1 / Passage-2' label is included in any context field. DATA SUFFICIENCY: items 48, 49 and 50 share identical boilerplate ('Which one of the following is correct in respect of the Question and the Statements?') and identical option sets. Their 'Question :' and 'Statement-1 / Statement-2' lines - and, for 48 and 50, their unique scenario preambles (circular table of six persons; six one-hour lectures between 8:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.) - are held in the STEM, not context, so the three items cannot collide on content_hash. Item 49 has no scenario preamble on the page and none was invented. PRINTED TEXT PRESERVED AS-IS, not corrected: (1) item 46 prints the decimal point of '1.25 times the first route' as a RAISED/MIDDLE dot (U+00B7) in the Indian typographic style - transcribed verbatim as '1·25', meaning is unambiguously one point two five; (2) page 30 Passage-2's closing clause reads 'the happiness that come our way' - 'come' where 'comes' is grammatically required. This is the booklet's own text and has been left uncorrected. Apostrophes have been written as ASCII (') rather than the printed curly quotes, because 2023-p2.merged.json already carries a U+FFFD replacement character from a smart quote at that position. No LaTeX was needed anywhere in this band: every variable (P, Q, X, Y, Z, A-F, x) occurs as a bare italic letter in running prose, never in an expression, matching the shipped convention of leaving such letters plain. Booklet header on all four pages: VGYH-D-CST/46A. No item numbers skip, none is duplicated, and no question in the band is defective.

questions.context: The demographic dividend, which has begun in India and is expected to last another few decades, is a great window of opportunity. The demographic dividend is basically a swelling in the working age population, which conversely means that the relative ratio of very young and very old will, for a while, be on the decline. From the experience of Ireland and China, we know that this can be a source of energy and an engine of economic growth. The demographic dividend tends to raise a nation's savings rate since in any nation, it is the working age population that is the main saver. And since the savings rate is an important driver of growth, this should help elevate our growth rate. However, the benefits of demographic dividend depend on the quality of the working age population. And this implies bringing back the importance of education, acquisition of skills and human capital.

questions.context: If presents bring less thrill now that we are grown up, perhaps it is because we have too much already; or perhaps it is because we have lost the fullness of the joy of giving, and with it the fullness of the joy of receiving. Children's fears are poignant, their miseries are acute, but they do not look too forward nor too far backward. Their joys are clear and complete, because they have not yet learnt always to add 'but' to every proposition. Perhaps we are too cautious, too anxious, too sceptical. Perhaps some of our cares would shrink if we thought less about them and entered with more single-minded enjoyment into the happiness that come our way.
